name: Holstrom Lakefront Parka
description:
A serious working parka designed for the brutal winter winds that come screaming off Lake Michigan through the Gray Zone and lower Tier 2 corridors. Cut long to the mid-thigh, it features a quilted recycled-fiber shell in faded olive or slate gray, with a massive hood that cinches down to a face-width opening via toggle cord. The exterior is treated with a durable water repellent finish that gets re-applied every season — or doesn't, and the coat just gets heavier when wet. Interior has two deep hand-warmer pockets and a chest pocket sized for a commlink. The stitching is thick and doubled at stress points.

Holstrom is a mid-tier Scandinavian-heritage brand that set up manufacturing in the corridor decades ago. Their parkas are not stylish. They are warm. The fill is a synthetic duck-down analog rated to minus twenty Celsius, and the outer fabric is tough enough to shrug off light debris and the occasional grabbed fence. the Gray Zone residents layer these over everything in winter. Couriers swear by them. You see them at bus stops, at processing plant gates, at Tier 2 market stalls — functional, honest, slightly shapeless.
what_it_says: You dress for the weather, not for appearances. Practicality over everything.
story_hooks: A courier's parka has a hidden interior seam that's been carefully unseamed and re-sewn — something was smuggled in the lining, and the coat changed hands before delivery

Holstrom quietly discontinued this model two seasons ago; remaining stock is selling fast, and a Tier 2 neighborhood collective is trying to pressure the company to resume production before winter hits
A character finds a name and a Tier 3 address written in permanent marker inside the collar — someone who used to own this coat lived very differently

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian mid-thigh-length parka with a commanding presence. The silhouette is deliberately boxy and unfitted—designed for layering and movement rather than form. The oversized hood dominates the upper profile, structured to collapse down into a face-width tunnel. Overall impression is rugged functionality: a garment that announces its purpose before aesthetics.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and spacious through the body, with room for thermal underlayers and utility belts. Sleeves are slightly tapered at the wrist for glove compatibility. The cut prioritizes freedom of movement and durability of stress points over any attempt at flattery.
physical_description.primary_material: Recycled-fiber quilted shell exterior; synthetic duck-down analog interior fill rated to -20°C. The outer layer is treated with a durable water-repellent (DWR) finish that degrades with time and re-application cycles.
physical_description.texture: The quilted exterior has a slightly quilted, padded topography visible across the entire jacket. The recycled-fiber weave is matte and textured—not smooth. With age and wear, the fabric develops a soft hand while maintaining structural integrity. Heavy stitching creates visible quilted lines that catch light.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded olive or slate gray—both colors chosen to hide stains and weathering. The dull, muted palette reads as 'this coat works, not plays.' Interior lining is typically darker, often charcoal or black.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty separating zipper (often brass or industrial-grade nylon) running full length. Magnetic snap closure at the chin level for quick face-sealing. The massive hood is cinched via thick braided toggle cord threaded through reinforced eyelets.
distinctive_features: Oversized, structural hood that collapses to face-width opening via braided toggle cord
Two deep hand-warmer pockets positioned for easy access through layers
Chest pocket sized specifically for commlink or other Tier 2/3 tech devices
Doubled and tripled stitching at all stress points (shoulders, underarms, hood attachment)
Exterior DWR coating that visibly degrades over seasons, creating a weathered patina
No visible branding except small woven Holstrom label at collar—understated
Interior construction is visible where coating has worn, showing quilting pattern and seam reinforcement
Sleeve cuffs are designed to overlay glove cuffs without bunching
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional wear. Not luxury, not salvage—this is the uniform of workers, couriers, and lower-management corpo staff who face the weather as part of their job.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing a Holstrom signals: 'I work outdoors in the GLMZ winter. I have a steady job. I don't have time for fashion, and I don't care.' It's a badge of the Gray Zone resident, Great Lakes laborer, courier network veteran. The parka says you understand the region's climate and have the stability to own proper gear.
physical_description.condition_typical: Parkas are worn broken-in: the DWR coating has dulled and patched, small tears are often rewoven rather than patched, the toggle cord may be frayed, interior lining shows creasing from repeated layering, stitching may be slightly visible where the outer shell has thinned from friction.
